_about: Every kind of PICTURE a person asks this product for, in the words they type, labelled with which of the product's three real mechanisms should serve it — or that none can and saying so is the right answer. Built 2026-09-28 for the 'a person can ask for a picture in many ways' survey, after the owner's flow-chart request was answered with 'attach the file again (CSV or Excel)'.
_provenance: One item is the owner's verbatim sentence as quoted in the programme brief (provenance=production). Every other item is authored for this evaluation. No conversation, database row or log was read: nothing here is user content.

_labels.chart-from-data: a real plot computed from a bound table. decide must want a file AND set chart_request.
_labels.diagram-in-chat: the model draws it as a ```mermaid fence in the answer. decide must make NO file, claim no chart, and refuse nothing.
_labels.diagram-in-file: a diagram inside a generated PDF/DOCX/PPTX. decide must want a file in the format the person named.
_labels.refuse-with-a-reason: this platform genuinely cannot draw it. decide must make no file AND name the visual so visuals.refusal_for can say why.
_labels.answer-about-a-file: the picture already exists — in an attachment or in a file we made. Read it back; draw nothing new.
_labels._route-corrects_tag: an item whose decide() verdict is overridden LOWER DOWN, by main.py._asks_about_an_attachment: with a PDF or an image on the turn the unsupported-visual refusal is skipped and the file is read. Scored, and reported apart, so a decide()-only number is not mistaken for what the person receives.

_kinds_doc: For each kind of picture: `mermaid` is the head from frontend/lib/mermaid.ts DIAGRAM_HEADS that the browser would draw it with ('' = none); `chart` is the chart_spec.CHART_TYPES id that draws it FROM A TABLE ('' = none); `in_file` is whether render/diagrams.py could carry it into a generated PDF/DOCX/PPTX — its _DIR_RE accepts `flowchart`/`graph` only, so every other mermaid kind is False even though the browser draws it.
_contexts_doc: ctx names a row of `contexts`; the scorer passes those keywords to intent.decide
_scoring_doc: score_pictures.py drives each item through intent.decide and grades the DECISION, not the wording of any answer: a chart-from-data item must end in a file with chart_request set; a diagram-in-chat item must end in NO file, with no chart claimed and nothing refused, so the model is free to emit a ```mermaid fence; a diagram-in-file item must end in a file in the format named; a refuse-with-a-reason item must end in no file AND name the visual, so visuals.refusal_for can say why.

N._doc: fresh chat: no table, no artifact, no previous answer. The ordinary way a diagram is asked for.

T._doc: an uploaded spreadsheet is in the conversation (the chat route's dataset_ready). The ordinary way a CHART is asked for.

A._doc: a substantial assistant ANSWER precedes this turn; no table, no file.

F._doc: a file the product made is already in the conversation (a report).

PDF._doc: a PDF is attached to THIS turn — the person is asking about a picture that already exists inside it.

chord.note: nothing draws it, and no word of it anywhere

picture.note: no image model on this platform
